events.quote: and - add another idea / but - show a contrast (something different) / because - give a reason

next_task.correct: The bus is cheap but it is slow.

errors.W1: The bus is cheap and it is slow.

events.quote: The rule: after he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb.
Right: She cooks pasta on Mondays. Wrong: She cook pasta on Mondays.
The rule: am, is or are + going to + verb talks about a plan.
Right: They are going to travel next week. Wrong: They going to travel next week.

next_task.correct: I am going to study tonight.

events.quote: we use a before a consonant sound (a book, a pen) and an before a vowel sound (an apple, an egg)
Rule: after "can", the action word stays simple, with no -s at the end.
Right: Tom can dance. Wrong: Tom can dances.
We use the when we talk about a thing again - the second time. First time: a. Second time: the.
'and' adds more, 'but' shows a contrast, 'because' gives a reason.

next_task.correct: The bus is cheap but it is slow.

errors.W1: The bus is cheap and it is slow.

events.quote: Irregular verbs have their own past form, so we don't add -ed: see -> saw, buy -> bought.
The rule: use many with things you can count, like eggs or books.
Right: She has many books. Wrong: She has much books.
Words like always, usually, sometimes and never come just before that verb.

next_task.correct: She goes to bed at ten.

events.quote: The present continuous is am/is/are + -ing. ... Don't forget is or are before the -ing verb!
We use it for things happening right now

events.quote: To talk about the weather, we use It is + adjective: It is sunny today.
Rule: use an before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u), and a before other sounds.
Right: I ate an egg. Wrong: I ate a egg.
We use am/is/are + verb-ing for actions happening now.
We use am/is/are + verb-ing for actions happening now.
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb.

Put always, usually, sometimes or never just before the action word.

events.quote: Many verbs make the past simple with -ed ... We use the past for finished actions, for example yesterday or last weekend.
I -> am ... he / she / it -> is ... you / we / they -> are
In English we must not leave this word out.

events.quote: Use many with things we can count (eggs, bottles). Use much with things we can't count (rice, milk).

Rule: after can, the action word has no s.

For plans we use am/is/are + going to + verb.
